name: Notion Guard
description:
Notion Guard is a governance-first Notion integration for small teams that want AI-assisted page and database work without silent or unrestricted changes.

It provides 10 focused commands for the real Notion REST API (2026-03-11, the data-source architecture introduced 2025-09-03): search across pages and data sources; inspect a data source's property schema; query/filter/sort a data source's rows; read a page's properties and its block content; list workspace users; create a page; update a page's properties or trash status; append content blocks to a page; and create a comment or reply to a discussion.

The six read commands are low-risk and execute immediately: they cannot alter workspace state, so gating them would only add friction. The four commands that change Notion (create_page, update_page_properties, append_blocks, create_comment) use RailCall's preview then approve then execute flow, and Notion is not changed until a human approves the exact payload.

notion.get_data_source_schema and notion.list_users exist for usability, not just coverage: the schema command lets a caller confirm real property names and select or status option values before writing, instead of guessing whether a field is named Status or Task Status, or whether a value is In Progress or In progress. notion.list_users lets people be addressed by name instead of raw UUIDs when setting an assignee (people) property.

Notion Guard uses the real Notion REST API with no mocks or stubs. Complex payloads (property values, block arrays, filters, sorts) are passed as JSON string fields so every write can express Notion's exact documented shapes rather than a lossy DSL. The handler checks HTTP status on every response, treats network failures and HTTP 5xx responses during a write as an unknown outcome instead of assuming success, never automatically retries a mutation, and does not present failed operations as successful results.

Quick start: install Notion Guard, create an internal integration at https://www.notion.so/my-integrations, share the relevant pages and databases with it, configure the integration secret through RailCall Studio, Integrations, Notion, reload Modules, and begin with notion.search to find a data source, then notion.get_data_source_schema before your first write. Preview every write before approving it.

Known limitations: the integration token acts with whatever pages and databases a workspace admin has explicitly shared with it. Notion Guard cannot see anything that has not been shared. Search, query, and content results are bounded to remain readable in RailCall receipts.

Built for the RailCall Track A module contest.

contest:2026Q3

Notion Guard declares zero model-provider destinations in its signed manifest. Its Notion REST traffic is the module's business integration path, not an LLM call, and the handler does not invoke any model-provider SDK or RailCall model-completion primitive.
